categories.name: The Bead's Moods
categories.tagline: How the bead and the glove look, sound and move, so a glance tells you more.

categories.name: More Than the Map Flag
categories.tagline: New things to point at, all drawn from the game's own sheets and your own character.

categories.name: Aetheryte to Doorstep
categories.tagline: Guidance that carries on past the teleport, across zone lines and back again.

categories.name: The Wayfinder's Linkpearl
categories.tagline: Sharing routes with friends and letting sibling plugins hear what the bead is doing.

ideas.title: A Colour for Every Source
ideas.pitch: The bead takes a different colour for your own target, the map flag and the quest step, so you always know which one it is following.
ideas.experience: You set a flag for a hunt mark while a quest is tracked. The bead turns the flag's red. You clear the flag and it fades to the quest's blue, and you know without opening the settings that it has moved on to the quest.
ideas.how: Configuration gains a colour per TargetSource beside BeadColor (which stays the default for Explicit). Overlay.DrawBead and DrawTrail pick the colour from scene.Guide.Target.Source; a Pulse.Approach blend over about 0.4 s eases the change. SettingsWindow gets three colour pickers and a 'one colour for all' box. Colors.cs already has Pack and Lighten.
ideas.risks: Three more colours to explain in a window that is already busy. Red and green as defaults would fail colour-blind players, so the defaults should differ in lightness too.
ideas.audience: everyone, especially players who keep a flag and a quest going at once

ideas.title: The Glove Warns of a Turn
ideas.pitch: With vnavmesh, the glove taps twice and leans into the next leg a few yalms before the path turns a corner.
ideas.experience: You run down a Limsa stairwell. Three yalms before the landing the glove taps twice and swings to the left, so you take the turn without overshooting and doubling back.
ideas.how: Navmesh already exposes Corner and the path's corners. In Overlay.DrawWalk, when the flat distance to path[Corner] falls under about 3 yalms, blend the glove's angle towards the next segment and run Pulse.Tap at double rate for one period. PathFollow gains a small pure helper for 'approaching corner' so it can be host-tested next to MotionAndPathTests.
ideas.risks: vnavmesh paths in towns have many short corners; the glove could fidget. Needs a minimum turn angle (say 30 degrees) before it warns. Not yet seen in game, like the rest of the path code.
ideas.audience: players who use vnavmesh paths, city navigators

ideas.title: Warmer, Colder
ideas.pitch: An optional soft chime that repeats faster as you face the right way and slows as you turn away, for players who would rather listen than look.
ideas.experience: You are looking at the market board chat, not the screen centre. A quiet chime ticks slowly, then quicker as you turn, then settles into a steady beat when you are on course. You walk there without once looking for the bead.
ideas.how: Heading.TurnAway already gives 0 to 1 for how far off course you face. A new pure Chime class in XivWayfinder.Core maps that and the distance to an interval, host-tested like Pulse. The plugin plays a game UI sound through FFXIVClientStructs' UIGlobals.PlaySoundEffect on each tick. Settings: off by default, a sound choice from the chat <se.1>-<se.16> set, and a volume note pointing at the game's own System Sounds slider.
ideas.risks: The game's sound effects cannot be pitched, so only the rate can carry meaning. Repeated chimes get tiring fast; it must stop on arrival and in the same situations Visibility.Decide hides the pointer. UIGlobals signatures can move between patches.
ideas.audience: low-vision players, players who hide most UI, screenshotters

ideas.title: A Glove on the Compass
ideas.pitch: A small glove clings to the edge of the minimap and points the way there too, for players who navigate by the minimap.
ideas.experience: You fly over Thavnair with the camera swung wide for the view. On the minimap's rim a tiny white glove sits at two o'clock, pointing out. It slides round the rim as you turn.
ideas.how: Read the _NaviMap addon's position, scale and rotation through IGameGui.GetAddonByName and its node tree. Place the glove on the ring with a circular version of ScreenEdge.RayToEdge (a new pure helper in Core, host-tested), and draw it with the existing Glove.Quad and GloveTexture, at a smaller size, on the same foreground draw list Overlay uses.
ideas.risks: The minimap can be locked north-up or to the camera, and its rotation must be read correctly for both. HUD layouts, scaling and minimap replacement plugins move or hide it. Addon node indices change between patches.
ideas.audience: minimap navigators, players with the camera zoomed right out

ideas.title: A Bead That Knows About Walls
ideas.pitch: Draw the bead in the world itself rather than on top of the screen, so a pillar or a companion can stand in front of it the way real things do.
ideas.experience: You round a column in the Crystarium and the bead slips out from behind it rather than floating in front of the stone. Its glow picks up the lamplight. It finally looks like part of the place.
ideas.how: Overlay draws everything on ImGui's foreground list, which has no depth. Two routes to try: spawn a client-side VFX at the bead's world position (the approach Splatoon-style plugins take), or read the game's depth buffer and test the bead's projected point against it before drawing. Either way the bead's position stays computed by Heading.Ahead and Pulse, and the ImGui bead remains the fallback.
ideas.risks: Both routes need hooks or signatures that break on patches, and a VFX left behind on unload or a crash stays in the scene. Reading the depth buffer is renderer-specific and may not work the same under Wine. May cost more frame time than the whole plugin does today.
ideas.audience: screenshotters, roleplayers, anyone bothered by overlays

ideas.title: Places You Keep
ideas.pitch: Save where you stand under a name and point back at it later: /wayfinder save forge, /wayfinder go forge.
ideas.experience: You find the quiet spot behind the Idyllshire inn where your FC meets. /wayfinder save meetup. A week later, logging in lost in the middle of Idyllshire, /wayfinder go meetup and the bead turns towards it, or names the aetheryte if you are elsewhere.
ideas.how: WayfinderCommands.Parse gains save, go, forget and places verbs (they must be matched before the free-text zone words). Configuration stores a list of (name, territory, x, y, z); names compare through ZoneMatch.Fold so accents and case do not matter. 'go' sets explicitTarget exactly as SetMapTargetFromCommand does, with the name as the label, so arrival, the aetheryte hint and GetState all work unchanged.
ideas.risks: A name that is also a zone name ('/wayfinder go limsa') needs a clear rule. Positions inside instanced housing are per ward and plot and would need those stored too, or be refused.
ideas.audience: roleplayers, gatherers, FC organisers, anyone who forgets where things are

ideas.title: A Queue of Stops
ideas.pitch: Line up several targets and walk them in order: each one is dropped as you reach it and the bead turns to the next.
ideas.experience: You have six vendors to visit for a crafting run. You paste six sets of coordinates, one after another, with /wayfinder add. The bead leads you to the first; on arrival chat says 'stop 1 of 6 reached' and the glove swings round to point at the second.
ideas.how: Plugin.explicitTarget becomes the head of an immutable list swapped atomically (IPC callers are on other threads). The existing ArrivalTimer and ClearOnArrival logic pop the head instead of clearing. New verbs in Commands.cs: add, next, skip, list. A new IPC function XivWayfinder.v1.AddTarget sits beside SetTarget in IpcContract.cs and docs/IPC.md; GetState gains a 'queue' count, which is additive and keeps version 1.
ideas.risks: The order is yours, not an optimised route; people will ask for 'shortest order', which is a travelling-salesman problem across zones. Queue and single-target semantics must stay obvious: does SetTarget replace the whole queue? It should, and the docs must say so.
ideas.audience: crafters, gatherers, sightseers, event hosts

ideas.title: Where Is the Mender?
ideas.pitch: Point at an NPC by name, /wayfinder find mender, using where the game's own data places them.
ideas.experience: Your gear is at 5% in Old Sharlayan and you have no idea where the mender stands. /wayfinder find mender. The bead turns, the distance reads 38 y, and a moment later you are repairing.
ideas.how: Build an index once from the Level sheet rows whose Type is an ENpc, joined to ENpcResident for names and titles ('Mender' is usually a title). Match with ZoneMatch's exact, then prefix, then substring ranking over ZoneMatch.Fold. Among placements pick the nearest in your zone first, like QuestPick.Nearest, else fall back to the aetheryte hint. Results become an Explicit Target with the NPC's name as the label, Y included so vnavmesh gets a proper floor.
ideas.risks: Many NPCs have several Level rows or appear only during certain quest phases, so the game data can place someone who is not there. Generic titles match dozens of NPCs. Building the index costs a noticeable moment on first use and must happen off the framework thread.
ideas.audience: returning players, new players, alts in unfamiliar cities

ideas.title: The Next Aether Current
ideas.pitch: Point at the nearest aether current in this zone that you have not yet attuned to.
ideas.experience: You land in a new zone and walk everywhere anyway. /wayfinder currents: the bead leads you up a ridge to a current you would have missed, then turns to the next one as soon as you have attuned.
ideas.how: The AetherCurrentCompFlgSet sheet lists each zone's currents; field currents are EObj placements found through Level rows. FFXIVClientStructs' PlayerState reports which currents are unlocked. A new source (or a queue fed into way-waypoint-queue) keeps the nearest unattuned one as the target, re-read at the same 0.25 s scan Plugin.Update already does for the flag and quest.
ideas.risks: Quest-rewarded currents have no field position and must be named, not pointed at. Plugins that already do this exist; this would need to be clearly nicer, not merely present. The EObj-to-current mapping has to be checked in game.
ideas.audience: levelling players, completionists, anyone unlocking flight

ideas.title: Sightseeing Log Guide
ideas.pitch: Point at the next Sightseeing Log vista you have not logged, and say which weather and hours it needs.
ideas.experience: The note above your head reads 'Vista 14: Clear Skies, 8 a.m. to noon'. It is raining, so you set it aside for later. Next morning the bead is already pointing at the cliff edge.
ideas.how: The Adventure sheet has each vista's Level (place), emote and time window; PlayerState knows which are complete. A new source reads them for the current expansion's log. The existing DrawNote glass note carries the conditions. Pure selection logic goes in Core with host tests, like QuestPick.
ideas.risks: Weather conditions come from another sheet and forecasting them is its own project. Needs care to not spoil vistas for players who like finding them unaided, so it only points at the one you ask for.
ideas.audience: completionists, sightseers, screenshotters

ideas.title: Towards the FATE
ideas.pitch: Follow the nearest active FATE in the zone, switching as FATEs start and end.
ideas.experience: You are grinding a relic step in Thanalan. A FATE pops on the far side of the map and the bead swings towards it. You arrive, the fight starts and the bead steps aside; when it ends the bead is already pointing at the next one.
ideas.how: Dalamud's IFateTable gives each active FATE's position and state. A fourth TargetSource, Fate, sits after Quest in TargetPicker.Pick, with its own toggle in SourceToggles and SettingsWindow. The existing combat rule in Visibility.Decide already hides the pointer while you fight.
ideas.risks: Adding a source touches the enum, IPC names in WayfinderIpc.Name and the GetState docs. FATE positions are what the map already shows, but a new source is still something to keep tidy. 'Nearest' flip-flops between two equal FATEs without hysteresis.
ideas.audience: relic and bicolour gem grinders, levelling players

ideas.title: X Marks the Spot
ideas.pitch: Once you have deciphered a timeworn map, point at the dig site it shows.
ideas.experience: You decipher a map and the little chart pops up. Instead of squinting at the landmarks, you close it and the note says 'Teleport to Camp Broken Glass'. When you land, the bead leads you straight to the spot.
ideas.how: The TreasureSpot and TreasureHuntRank sheets give the candidate Level rows; which one is yours is only known after deciphering. Research whether the client exposes it in an agent (as the treasure-map UI must know it) before considering a hook. The result becomes an Explicit Target, so the aetheryte hint and vnavmesh work unchanged.
ideas.risks: If the spot is only in a network packet, reading it means a hook, which is fragile and a larger step than anything the plugin does now. Established plugins already fill this niche. Must never extend to anything the player has not deciphered themselves.
ideas.audience: treasure hunters, map parties

ideas.title: The Quest Continues Next Door
ideas.pitch: When a quest step lies on another map, point at the exit the game's own quest link names instead of just saying 'another zone'.
ideas.experience: Your next step is in Western Thanalan and you are standing in Central Thanalan. Instead of 'Teleport to Horizon', the glove points down the road to the zone exit, the same way the game's own map arrow does.
ideas.how: docs/WAYFINDER.md lists AgentMap.MapQuestLinkContainer (QuestId, LevelId, source and target map) as 'not used yet'. GameReader.Quest reads it when no marker or to-do Level is in the player's zone and returns the link's Level as the target, labelled with the destination. Core gains a pure chooser beside QuestPick.Nearest, host-tested.
ideas.risks: The container reflects what the map has loaded, the same known gap the event markers have. Links can point at places the player can only reach by ferry or NPC. Needs checking against a real journal, which nothing in the quest reads has had yet.
ideas.audience: questing players, returning players on long MSQ runs

ideas.title: Walk, Don't Teleport
ideas.pitch: When the target is one or two zones away on foot, point at the zone exit instead of naming an aetheryte.
ideas.experience: Your flag is in Middle La Noscea, just over the line from where you stand. The note offers a choice: 'Teleport to Summerford Farms' or the glove pointing at the road east, 'on foot, 1 zone'.
ideas.how: Map-to-map links come from MapMarker rows of the map-link type, read the same way GameReader.AetherytesIn already reads aetheryte markers and converted with MapCoords.PixelToWorld. Build a zone graph once and find the shortest walk with a breadth-first search in Core (pure, host-tested). TargetPicker.Plan grows a WalkToExit guide kind; GetState's 'guide' field gains a value, documented in IPC.md.
ideas.risks: Links through ferries, airships and NPC dialogue are not walkable and are hard to tell apart from real exits. One-way drops and locked zones (before a quest opens them) will mislead. Deciding when walking beats teleporting is a judgement call, so the first version should only offer it for adjacent zones.
ideas.audience: players saving gil, sprouts, roleplayers who like to walk

ideas.title: The Aethernet Leg
ideas.pitch: In the big cities, name the aethernet shard nearest the target as well: 'Teleport to Ul'dah, then aethernet to Sapphire Avenue Exchange'.
ideas.experience: Your target is the Ul'dah market. The note says 'Teleport to Ul'dah, then aethernet to Sapphire Avenue Exchange'. You arrive by the shard and the bead is waiting, pointing across the plaza.
ideas.how: The Aetheryte sheet includes aethernet shards (not IsAetheryte, grouped by AethernetGroup), with MapMarker positions like the main aetherytes. Extend GameReader.AetherytesIn to return shards, and TargetPicker.NearestAetheryte to pick a (main, shard) pair when the shard saves real distance. Also useful in the same zone: 'aethernet to X' when the walk is long.
ideas.risks: Shard attunement state needs its own check, and it may not be exposed as simply as IAetheryteList. Cities span several territories (Ul'dah Steps of Nald and Thal), so the shard graph crosses zones. The note gets longer and must stay readable.
ideas.audience: everyone who gets lost in Ul'dah, city shoppers

ideas.title: Pointing on the Wing
ideas.pitch: When you are mounted and flying, ask vnavmesh for a flight path and let the bead climb and dive with it.
ideas.experience: You take off in Il Mheg. The bead drifts upwards with you, points over the treeline rather than round it, and dips as you approach the flag so you know when to descend.
ideas.how: Navmesh.Request always passes fly = false to vnavmesh.Nav.PathfindCancelable. Pass true when ICondition shows InFlight (and Diving under water), and requery on take-off and landing through PathFollow.ShouldRequery. Heading.Ahead gains a pitched variant so the bead follows the path's height; the glove stays a ground-plane pointer with an up or down hint.
ideas.risks: vnavmesh's flight meshes are less tested than its ground meshes. A flying path to a flag without height has no obvious end altitude. Must stay pointing only: never vnavmesh's movement gates, in the air as on the ground.
ideas.audience: flyers, gatherers, hunt trains

ideas.title: Breadcrumbs Back
ideas.pitch: Remember the way you came and point you back along it: /wayfinder back.
ideas.experience: You chased a gathering node deep into a Kholusian cave and lost your bearings. /wayfinder back, and a trail of small beads lights up the route you walked in, leading you out the way you came.
ideas.how: Plugin.Update records your own position into a fixed ring buffer every couple of yalms (allocation-free, covered by AllocationBudgetTests), cleared on zone change. 'back' feeds the reversed crumbs to the existing PathFollow.NextCorner as if they were a vnavmesh path, and DrawTrail shows them. Nothing but your own character is recorded, and nothing is saved to disk.
ideas.risks: Crumbs recorded while flying or swimming do not make a walkable path. Loops and backtracking need simplifying, or the bead leads you round every detour you made. Zone changes break the trail.
ideas.audience: gatherers, explorers, players who get lost in caves and cities

ideas.title: Arrival and Change Events
ideas.pitch: Tell other plugins when a target is reached or changes, so Ghostty, XivMcp or a macro plugin can react without polling GetState.
ideas.experience: XivMcp set a target for you from a question you asked. When you arrive, it hears the arrival at once and follows up in its own window with the next thing you wanted, instead of checking every second.
ideas.how: Two message gates next to the existing four in IpcContract.cs: XivWayfinder.v1.Arrived (label, territory) and XivWayfinder.v1.StateChanged (the same JSON as WayfinderIpc.StateJson), sent with ICallGateProvider.SendMessage from Plugin.Update when the arrival timer fires or the guide kind or target changes. docs/IPC.md documents them, and the existing host test that checks every contract name is in the doc covers them.
ideas.risks: StateChanged must be debounced or it fires every frame the distance changes. Subscribers run on the framework thread and a slow one could stall it; the docs must say to return quickly.
ideas.audience: plugin authors, XivMcp and Ghostty users

ideas.title: Treasure Hunt Routes
ideas.pitch: Build a route of stops with a riddle at each and share it as a pasteable code, so an FC can run a scavenger hunt with nothing but chat.
ideas.experience: Your FC's event host posts a short code in FC chat. You paste it with /wayfinder route. The note shows the first riddle: 'where the bell tolls over sand'. When you reach the right spot a soft ring blooms, the next riddle appears and the bead turns towards the next stop.
ideas.how: A route is a small JSON list of (territory, x, z, label, clue, hidden) compressed and base64-encoded with a version prefix; parsing and validation go in Core using WayfinderIpc.Validate and CleanLabel for every stop, so a malicious code can do nothing but point. Builds on way-waypoint-queue. 'Hidden' stops show no bead until the previous one is reached, only the clue in DrawNote. Recording a route is /wayfinder route add at each spot. No network: the code is passed by hand.
ideas.risks: Codes get long for many stops and chat limits message length. Hidden stops can be cheated by reading the code, which is fine for fun and should be said plainly. Clues are player-written text, so they need the same cleaning labels get.
ideas.audience: FC event hosts, roleplay communities, friend groups

ideas.title: The Proving Ground
ideas.pitch: A step-by-step window that walks you through the in-game checks in docs/WAYFINDER.md and builds a report to paste into an issue.
ideas.experience: You install the dev plugin and open /wayfinder prove. Step 1 ticks itself when the test target shows at about 20 yalms. At step 7 you tick 'aims round the wall' by hand. At the end one button copies a tidy report with your status lines, glove and vnavmesh state and game version.
ideas.how: A new window beside SettingsWindow, with the eight steps from 'Proving it in game' as data. Steps that can be checked automatically read WayfinderState (guide Walk, distance close to 20, source Flag, source Quest, Navmesh true, reason 'cutscene'); the others are manual ticks. The report joins WayfinderIpc.StatusLine, GloveTexture.Status and Navmesh.Status and goes to the clipboard, never the network.
ideas.risks: An automatic tick proves only what the plugin believes, not what the player saw, so the report must keep the two kinds of evidence apart. The step list must stay in step with the doc.
ideas.audience: testers, early adopters, the author before a release
